Retrieved T2DM Medical Knowledge & Guidelines:
[ADA Standards of Care (2024) - Glycemic Targets]:
An HbA1c goal of < 7.0% (53 mmol/mol) is appropriate for many non-pregnant adult patients with Type 2 Diabetes to prevent or slow microvascular complications (retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy). Stringent targets (< 6.5%) may be considered for younger patients with short diabetes duration, long life expectancy, and no significant cardiovascular disease if achievable without significant hypoglycemia or adverse treatment effects. Less stringent targets (< 8.0% or 8.5%) are indicated for patients with a history of severe hypoglycemia, limited life expectancy, advanced microvascular or macrovascular complications, extensive comorbid conditions, or long-standing diabetes difficult to control. HbA1c reflects average glycemia over approximately 90-120 days, weighted towards the preceding 30 days. Conditions that alter red blood cell turnover (hemoglobinopathies, severe anemia, hemodialysis) require plasma glucose or fructosamine evaluation.
Citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024, Diabetes Care 2024;47(Suppl. 1):S111–S125

[Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) & ADA Standards (2023-2024) - Comprehensive Medical Evaluation and Assessment of Comorbidities]:
Routine laboratory monitoring for T2DM patients includes: 1. HbA1c testing at least twice yearly in patients meeting glycemic goals and stable regimens; quarterly in patients whose therapy has changed or who are not meeting goals. 2. Serum creatinine and calculated estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) at least annually (every 3–6 months if eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m2). 3. Spot urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) annually to detect early diabetic kidney disease. 4. Fasting lipid panel (Total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, Triglycerides) annually, or every 4-12 weeks following initiation or adjustment of lipid-lowering therapy. 5. Liver function enzymes (AST, ALT) annually, especially given high prevalence of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH). 6. Serum potassium and electrolytes when prescribed ACE inhibitors, ARBs, SGLT2 inhibitors, or diuretics.
Citation: ICMR Guidelines for Management of Type 2 Diabetes 2023, Ch. 3; ADA Standards 2024, Section 4

[World Health Organization (WHO) & ADA Standards (2023-2024) - Glycemic Monitoring & Clinical Targets]:
Target preprandial (fasting) capillary blood glucose for non-pregnant adults with T2DM is 80–130 mg/dL (4.4–7.2 mmol/L). Peak postprandial capillary blood glucose (measured 1–2 hours after the start of a meal) target is < 180 mg/dL (< 10.0 mmol/L). Fasting hyperglycemia predominantly reflects excessive hepatic glucose output and basal insulin deficiency, whereas postprandial hyperglycemia reflects impaired first-phase insulin secretion and peripheral insulin resistance following carbohydrate ingestion. Marked discordance between HbA1c and fasting glucose often indicates postprandial glycemic excursions. Self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) frequency should be tailored to medication regimen: higher frequency with insulin/secretagogues, and structured periodic testing for non-insulin regimens.
Citation: WHO Package of Essential NCD Interventions 2023; ADA Standards of Care 2024, Section 6
